shared_elements: tall upright monolithic stone block as the carved support
carving in shallow relief on the stone face
suggestion of arms/hands rendered in low relief on the body of the stone
vertical composition with an emphasized upper zone (head/top register)
justification: Both are tall, roughly rectangular upright stone monoliths whose carving concentrates in an upper zone and continues down the shaft, and each shows arm-like relief elements running down the body, which is the most specific correspondence. Otherwise they diverge sharply: A is a volumetric, fully three-dimensional head-and-torso figure with modelled facial features in coarse granular stone, while B is a flat pillar covered in shallow, linear low-relief registers of animals (birds, a quadruped, a snake-like form) and geometric banding, with no face at all.
